correctness.rationale: For |a| strictly between zero and one, the corrected iterate is an absolutely trace-norm convergent series of Fock derivative-jet rank-one operators. Exterior powers have the unique leading multi-index 1,...,j, and their norms yield the product of the first j singular values. The two successive wedge Gram pivots are computed exactly by a truncated reproducing kernel and a Weyl unitary; their product gives the claimed coefficient for each fixed j. Gaussian binomial bounds control the infinite expansion, while 456 exact rational checks independently confirm the polynomial and finite Gram algebra. Complex phases enter only through t=a^n and |c|. A finite checker does not replace the analytic proof.

For the corrected iterate, the exact fixed-rank coefficient is e^{|c|^2/2}(1+|c|^{2j}/(j!K_{j-1}(c,c))). It is rank-dependent and, for j=1 with c nonzero, has the extra factor 1+|c|^2. Thus the new claim is not implied by simply deleting the largest known singular value of C_phi^n; a new nonorthogonal dual-jet calculation is required.

originality.rationale: The focal 2021 paper establishes convergence but no fixed-rank corrected-error singular spectrum. The 2022 approximation-number theorem concerns the uncorrected compact composition operator, whose singular numbers do not determine those of its difference with a generally nonorthogonal rank-one projection. An exact Fock-jet coefficient for every fixed rank is not implied by either inspected statement. Matching published-finding corpus output was not found by actual semantic claim and alias searches; limited bibliographic access to an earlier 2017 approximation-number source remains a priority risk.

value.rationale: For a natural long-time analytic composition dynamics that was previously only known to converge to a rank-one map, the theorem supplies every fixed-rank optimal approximation error with sharp exponential rate and explicit nonorthogonal jet constant. The rank-dependent Poisson partial sums measure fixed-point distortion; this structure is not the geometric spectrum of the original compact operator. The result gives a reproducible hierarchy useful for finite-rank approximation of iterative Fock sampling, without requiring a downstream general theorem.
